DILG BAGONG PILIPINAS Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City OPINION NO. JUN 112025 MR. RONALD CAMIT Imus, Cavite Ronald.camit@aon.com Dear Mr. Camit: This has reference to your electronic mail dated 23 October 2024 seeking this Department's guidance regarding the obligation of Punong Barangays in serving the summons in a civil case. According to the representation, you are a complainant in a civil lawsuit filed before the Courts of Region VIII, where the Defendants are allegedly hiding. You then stated that you asked the Punong Barangay of a certain barangay in an unnamed municipality in Region VIII if you might appoint her as your representative to serve the summons via substituted service. You stated that the Punong Barangay rejected your request for assistance in serving the summons, citing that the case had already been filed in court. You also alleged that the Punong Barangay is protecting the defendants and lacks a sense of justice and public duty. In this regard, you seek clarification on whether the Punong Barangay has a legal obligation to assist in serving the summons in a civil case. Section 5(d) of Republic Act No. 6713, otherwise known as the Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards for Public Officials and Employees, mandates that all public officials and employees must attend to individuals seeking their services and must, at all times, act promptly and expeditiously. However, it is important to clarify that the Punong Barangay's obligation to serve summons is primarily within the jurisdiction of the Katarungang Pambarangay system, as provided under Chapter VII, Title I, Book III of the Local Govemment Code of the Philippines. Civil cases filed in regular courts fall outside the authority of barangay officials, and the service of summons in such cases must follow formal court procedures as prescribed by the Rules of Court. Accordingly, while the Punong Barangay is expected to provide assistance to the community in general, the service of summons in a civil case pending before the courts is not within his/her legal duty. Such service must be carried out by the proper court officers in accordance with established judicial processes. "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

This opinion is rendered based solely on the facts and representations stated in your letter and our appreciation thereof. We hope this sufficiently addresses your concerns. Thank you. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: ATTY. ROMEO P. BENITEZ Undersecretary for External,Legal and Legislative Affairs OUSELLNJVRULLLS-LRALLD/lasm copy FURNISHED: ARIEL O.
